title: Live account results from my AI-assisted trading model since March - up 41%
author: Homebody_quant
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/e1w9twi943ih1.png?width=2585&format=png&auto=webp&s=5930ef6ed4e9c003dacc629c917abdc95951ecbb

|Period|Holdings|
|:-|:-|
|April|GEV, LITE, LRCX, STX, WDC|
|May|LITE, MU, SNDK, STX, WDC|
|June|INTC, MU, SNDK, STX, WDC|
|July|INTC, MU, SNDK, STX, WDC|
|August|CRWD, CSCO, DELL, GOOGL, PANW|

I’ve been live trading my own AI-assisted stock model since March and wanted to share an update.  The live portfolio is up 41.3% from Mar 23 to Aug 7.  

The live account has real fills, partial sizing that does not perfectly match the model weights, timing differences, and manual execution friction.  I am just a person who logs in the day before then buys at 'market' price.  Could it be optimized further.... yeah, probably, but it is really easy to get the decision at night after the last day of the month, then set the sell order for the morning, then buy and go about my day. 

I am exploring if I can just fully port this into a raspberry pi and let it run on its own with minimal oversight.

comments.author: krazineurons
comments.body: So your model is helping predict which stocks to enter before they start showing price movement?

replies.author: Homebody_quant
replies.body: It essentially follows winners. Or tries to

comments.author: Natemare141
comments.body: Curious to hear more about the momentum via public data only side

replies.author: Homebody_quant
replies.body:
Not sure how to address it? 
Part of the thesis is that SEC filings are delayed and even then its hard to filter out winners. 13F is good but again hard to translate into a strategy and the release of the disclosures makes it less ideal.  

Also theres just far too many people and players that can impact the price. I am just trying to follow what they are doing like a crowd.

comments.author: Ok-Draft2744
comments.body: Since you are using a momentum strategy/algo, how is your system assisted by AI? What is AI doing for you that is adding value?

replies.author: Homebody_quant
replies.body: Its not a fully automated system yet but it assists in the building and execution.  I manually trade it for now.  Slowly shifting into fully automated trades.

comments.author: hikewithcaramel
comments.body: If you have a list of instruments and a strategy, what is the LLM doing? Could your entry and exit plan be hard coded? What does the LLM bring to the party?

replies.author: Homebody_quant
replies.body: No llm.  It introduces variability which makes it tough to test and replicate.     Its a hard coded strategy.  The goal is to eventually automate the trading and full port into algotrading

replies.author: hikewithcaramel
replies.body: Good luck with it. I'm going to post my project up here soon. Watch out for it. Keep us updated

replies.body:
Thanks.

I will keep an eye out for the post.

replies.author: Homebody_quant

comments.author: CloutChaserv4
comments.body:
Very cool! I started trading a similar strategy I call [CloutChaser v4](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/s/9MVKte65ro) literally this week!

Can you share some details on your development and backtesting process? When I developed CCv4 this kind of sector concentration resulted in huge drawdowns, so I had to basically develop an annual process to hand-pick the universe of potential stocks based on their sector, liquidity, market cap, trading history and other factors. Can you speak generally about how you select your candidates?

Thanks for sharing!

replies.author: Homebody_quant
replies.body:
Definitely interesting.  Jegadeesh and Titman are core influences.  It seems that it might be similar.   

The selection process is dynamic to handle a variety of regimes and does a good job of screening.
